top_signals.title: The U.S.-Chinese-Russian Summit and the Future of Trilateral Nuclear Talks
top_signals.summary:
U.S. President Donald Trump, who has sought nuclear arms control with Russia and China since his first term, may finally have his chance. The first-ever U.S.-Chinese-Russian leaders’ summit is set to take place in Shenzhen, with nuclear issues potentially on the agenda. Regardless of whether the summit yields substantive progress, it could make the prospect of trilateral nuclear arms control seem somewhat less remote than before. For Beijing, however, the summit’s symbolism matters most: Washington is finally treating its geopolitical and ideological adversaries as equals in addressing issues of global governance.
